discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Bloch, Esslinger and Greiner turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into precise analogue quantum simulators of condensed-matter models. Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition of the Bose-Hubbard model (2002). Esslinger pioneered fermions in optical lattices, imaging Fermi surfaces and realising the fermionic Mott insulator of the Hubbard model (2008), as did Bloch's group. Greiner and Bloch then invented quantum gas microscopes with single-site, single-atom resolution, which revealed antiferromagnetic correlations, string order and entanglement directly in real space. These methods made it possible to answer open questions about strongly correlated electrons, including high-temperature superconductivity and magnetism, by direct measurement in clean, tunable systems. Laboratories worldwide now use them as standard tools, and they underpin today's programmable neutral-atom quantum simulators and processors. Together, these achievements opened a new experimental route into quantum many-body physics.
